messages:
laura: quick heads-up — hit an OOM while running an incremental backfill of indexless safetensors into the shared cache. trying to sketch a small "backfill shim" idea that avoids a full manifest rewrite and still satisfies the loader's 'index-first' checks.

laura: problem statement: some checkpoints are stored as raw safetensors shards (no sidecar index). loader path expects an index or manifest for streaming and hotstart; without it we either do full in-memory indexing or fall back to slow range reads that blow memory/latency.

sam: can you paste the failure log? is it hitting memory during parsing or during the write to the cache? :thinking_face:

laura: parsing + assembling small per-shard header map. sample log: ```ERROR: shard-17 parse OOM at parse_tensor_headers()\nTrace: ... alloc 1.2GB for header_map```

nate: oof. two thoughts: 1) produce a tiny on-disk manifest that only lists per-shard byte ranges + checksums (no full tensor table). 2) let the runtime accept a streaming 'header stub' that contains only what the hotstart path needs (kv offsets + dtype/shape).

irene: +1 for header stubs. we already have warmup logic that only needs offsets to prime KV cache. if backfill shim can atomically write a stub then loader will fast-path. need atomic rename to avoid races.

mike: caveat: some legacy loaders verify a magic footer/manifest hash at load-time. if we synthesize a partial manifest we need a compatibility header or version tag. otherwise we get checksum mismatches and reject the shard.

laura: good call. proposal: backfill shim writes a companion file <shard>.stub.json with minimal fields: version, shard_index, offsets[], checksum. then atomic rename to <shard>.stub.json.ready (or vice-versa). loader accepts stub if present and uses range-reads for missing tensor spans. example stub:```{\n  \"version\": \"0.1\",\n  \"shard\": 17,\n  \"offsets\": [0, 128, 10240],\n  \"checksum\": \"sha256:abcd...\"\n}```

anya: how do we decide when to synthesize vs fully index? cost tradeoffs. my vote: synthesize for shards < 10GB or where IO latency is high; schedule full manifest async and garbage-collect stubs when finished.

sam: also consider a size-limited parser: stream headers and write offsets to disk as you go (O(1) memory). that removes OOM but still yields a proper manifest over time. shim can be the streaming parser with a 'give up after X MB in memory' policy and fall back to stub.

nate: also think about eviction/consistency. if we write a stub that says offsets but the underlying shard changes (reupload), we need a provenance check. include upload-time nonce or object ETag in stub. loader checks it before trusting.

irene: +1 for ETag. for atomicity, we can use an overlay pattern: write stub.tmp -> fsync -> rename to stub. Then publish a tombstone for old stubs if shard replaced.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/loader-stub-checks -> staging at 2026-03-25T03:00Z :rocket: (contains stub read/accept logic, no write side yet)

laura: outstanding UX questions: 1) where do we surface stub vs manifest in catalog? 2) metrics to know how many requests hit stub-path and latency delta?

anya: catalog: add a 'index_state' field: {indexed, stubbed, none}. metrics: per-route histogram tag index_state. easy to add in console.

mike: security/compliance: stubs are derived from the same shard bytes, so no new PHI risk. but we must ensure stubs respect KMS encryption markers if store encrypts at rest (stubs should not leak unencrypted offsets). offsets are not secret but follow internal policy. add an audit entry when stub created.

laura: action items: Sam to prototype streaming parser fallback (low-memory) by EOW; Anya to spec index_state + metrics; Nate to add ETag provenance checks; Irene to add atomic write pattern to loader acceptance docs. I'll start a tiny PoC for stub writer that targets S3 and local FS.

laura: thanks everyone — want to avoid a large refactor but still unblock hotstarts. if any objections ping me — otherwise i'll open a short RFC with the decisions later today. :+1:
